newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA COULD CALL ON RONALDO FOR CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA COULD CALL ON RONALDO FOR CUP FINAL.

text.p: Barcelona president Jose Luis Nunez said on Monday that Brazilian striker Ronaldo still belonged to the club and could be called on to play in the Spanish Cup final.
It signalled another twist in Ronaldo's complicated move to Internazionale of Italy.
Ronaldo's lawyer had on Friday paid the four billion pesetas ($27.6 million) theoretically needed to make him a free agent.
But Nunez maintained: "He's still a club player."
At the same time, the Spanish Football Federation, citing a FIFA circular, reaffirmed its refusal to allow Inter to sign Ronaldo without negotiating with Barcelona.
Nunez said he would wait to see if Brazil qualified for the final of the Copa America before deciding whether or not to call upon Ronaldo for Barcelona's Spanish Cup final against Real Betis.
Barcelona's position has been boosted by the confirmation of the Federation's stance.

The Federation has been informed by FIFA that the payment of 'withdrawal clauses' stipulated in Spanish contracts is valid only for transfers within the country and that moves abroad must be negotiated.
"As the situation is, we cannot allow Ronaldo to move to Inter unless the Italian club talks to Barcelona," Federation press secretary Fernando Garrido told Reuters.
Negotiations between Barcelona and the striker's agents broke down last month.
